messages:
leah: Quick RFC follow-up — who owns the final evict/rollback decision for canaries: local runtime or central controller? Need a practical, low-risk default.
omar: My leaning: hybrid. Local for immediate hard stops, central for measured rollbacks. But we must define clear contracts.
vik: Hybrid sounds right. Key constraints: 1) observability continuity (central must reconstruct what local saw), 2) bounded local authority (so a buggy runtime can't mass-evict).
priya: Implementation constraints: central has higher-latency but global view. Local has speed. So local should only hard-evict on extreme thresholds (safety limits). Everything else should flow to central arbitration.
fallback-bot: canary: id=cnry-2026-03-21T14:02 started size=3% region=ap-south :rocket:
leah: Proposed contract: - local_hard_thresholds (emergency only) - local_advisories (non-binding signals sent to controller) - controller_decision_ttl (controller can override within Xs) - signed_overrides + audit.
omar: For telemetry: local sends compact fingerprints every 5s: {ts, err_slice, p95_delta, sample_count, seq}. Controller stores a rolling window and replays decisions. Keep payload <1KB per canary shard.
vik: Also require a min_samples guard: controller won't act on a variant unless sample_count >= min_samples_in_window (default 250). This avoids oscillation from tiny cohorts.
priya: Soft vs hard: soft = stop routing new sessions; hard = terminate in-flight + drain replacement. Default soft for A/B, default hard only when local_hard_threshold breached or controller explicitly requests hard.
leah: Example manifest fragment to encode behavior:
```yaml
canary:
  fallback_policy:
    mode: hybrid
    local_hard_thresholds:
      error_rate_pct: 15
      p95_latency_ms: 4000
    min_samples: 250
    controller_reclaim_window_s: 50
    telemetry_profile: compact_fingerprint
```
omar: Tie-breaker rules: if local and controller disagree within reclaim window, controller decision wins unless local indicates "safety-critical" with signed proof (seq + metrics_signature). That keeps central authoritative but respects local emergency.
vik: Deterministic conflict resolution: decisions carry monotonic decision_id (controller or runtime) and priority enum {safety, controller, advisory}. Compare by priority then decision_id. Keep lexicographic ordering if needed.
priya: Observability requirements for Console: show last_local_decision, last_controller_decision, cohesion_lag_ms (median+95), and a linkable decision_trace (metrics fingerprint + reason). Add alert when cohesion_lag_ms > 1500ms for >2 windows.
leah: Security: overrides must be mutual-TLS + signed token. Controller signs decisions with key-id header; runtime verifies and records provenance in audit logs. No self-approval for cross-tenant rollbacks.
omar: Test matrix: simulate central-unavailable + local spike -> local hard threshold triggers, ensure controller when back online can reconcile state and (a) acknowledge, (b) rollback if local was false positive. Add chaos tests for jitter and skewed clocks.
vik: On oscillation: include decay on score and a cooldown after soft-fallback before allowing re-eval (e.g., 10m cooldown or until sample_count returns to baseline). Also require at least 2 consecutive windows over threshold for controller-triggered global evict.
priya: Dev notes: provide /v1/decisions endpoint on runtime that returns decision history and metrics_signature for each decision. Controller posts /v1/override with signed TTL. Keep overrides idempotent.
leah: UX: manifest UI should display current owner (local/controller) with a one-click handback and a history of recent overrides. PMs want a readable one-line explanation for any auto-evict.
omar: Action items: 1) draft runtime decision API spec @vik, 2) compact fingerprint schema @priya, 3) manifest schema changes PR @omar, 4) chaos tests for central outage @leah.
vik: I'll take API spec.
priya: I'll mock telemetry schema and sample test payloads.

leah: Great. I'll consolidate this thread into a short RFC addendum and call out the safety thresholds so we can land manifest changes. Thanks all. :memo:
